note.en: Rack-scale product with very limited on-demand access: CoreWeave still lists the cheapest published rate (~$10.50/GPU-hr), while the tracked provider average has drifted up to ~$17-18/GPU-hr as more enterprise-only listings entered pricing indexes; hyperscaler bare-metal (Azure) tops out at ~$27/GPU-hr. Most capacity (Together AI, Oracle, Azure) is still sold as reserved contracts with quote-only pricing.

Min holds at Vultr's ~$3.50/GPU-hr; typical on-demand ticked up to ~$6.50/GPU-hr as specialized neoclouds (Vast.ai, Hyperbolic, Hyperstack) cluster $5.90-7.20 alongside pricier Lambda/Nebius/CoreWeave listings, while Google Cloud's a4-highgpu-8g stays the ceiling at $16.11/GPU-hr. No clean published 1-year rate.

Newest AMD flagship with a thin rental market: Vultr's 8x pods remain the floor at ~$2.59/GPU-hr, but the typical price has drifted up sharply to ~$7.15/GPU-hr as OVHcloud (~$7.10) and CoreWeave (~$7.20) on-demand became the more representative listings, with Oracle bare metal still topping the range at $8.60/GPU-hr. CoreWeave's 1-year reservation holds at $4.25/GPU-hr — a ~41% discount to its own on-demand rate. Coverage is still thin (3-4 tracked providers), so treat the median move as directional.

Min from FluidStack ($2.30, unchanged), typical neocloud range clusters at $4.11-4.15 (getdeploying, AIMultiple), but the hyperscaler ceiling nearly doubled to ~$13.78/GPU-hr as Azure's ND96isr H200 v5 became directly listed. Reserved-rate listings still average ~$3.72/GPU-hr.

Widest rental market (48+ providers): marketplace/neocloud low end still $1.49/GPU-hr (Vast.ai), typical price holds near $3.35/GPU-hr (AIMultiple, GetDeploying). The hyperscaler ceiling shifted to Azure's ND96isr H100 v5 (~$12.29/GPU-hr, $98.32/hr ÷ 8 GPUs), overtaking Google Cloud's a3-highgpu-8g (~$11.06/GPU-hr, unchanged). Per SemiAnalysis, 1-year contract rates hold around $2.35/GPU-hr after their spring-2026 rebound.

sources.label: Vantage — Azure ND96isr H100 v5 instance pricing

note.en: Aggressively priced for its 192GB of HBM3: TensorWave anchors the low end at ~$1.71/GPU-hr, while Azure/Oracle's 8x on-demand list price tops the range at $6.00/GPU-hr (revised down from a previously tracked $7.86 after checking Azure's own pricing page directly). Cyfuture AI publishes a 12-month reserved rate of $1.82/GPU-hr; prices trending down as MI355X arrives.

Legacy workhorse in steady decline: Thunder Compute now undercuts the field at ~$1.09/GPU-hr, RunPod/Lambda cluster at $1.39-2.79, with GCP a2-ultragpu still listing ~$5.07/GPU-hr at the top. No widely published 1-year rate; most contract demand has moved to H100/H200.

TensorDock now anchors the low end at ~$0.47/GPU-hr (Verda's own listed rate has since risen well above this). Typical pricing has drifted down to ~$1.27/GPU-hr as more budget-tier neocloud listings (Packet AI, GPU Outlet, Beam, Latitude.sh, all $0.54-0.90) entered the tracked market, and the hyperscaler ceiling holds at Oracle Cloud's ~$3.50/GPU-hr. No standard published 1-year rates.

Consumer flagship on marketplaces only (no hyperscaler offering): Salad Cloud now the floor at ~$0.27/GPU-hr, RunPod Secure Cloud unchanged at $0.99 the published top. Typical pricing (AIMultiple) ticked up slightly to ~$0.56/GPU-hr. Supply growing through 2026, pushing prices toward RTX 4090 levels.

Vast.ai's marketplace floor has slipped further to ~$0.13/GPU-hr (from ~$0.18-0.20), while serverless-billed providers keep the ceiling near $1.61/GPU-hr (GetDeploying/AIMultiple aggregate) as Beam-style endpoint configs list up to $1.77/GPU-hr. Typical pricing holds steady around $0.48/GPU-hr — RunPod Secure Cloud's $0.69 remains well off the tracked reference points on either side.
